source: Source-separated ERA5 and NASA POWER studies
mode: walk-forward evaluation and separate full-data refit

protocol.method: Six expanding-window, whole-year blocks; earlier stopping and calibration windows; held-out evaluation in May only.
protocol.calibration: Two immediately preceding May years; F1 threshold selected on calibration only. Selection uses the earlier two May years.
protocol.target: nagpur-grid-proxy-v1 rule; fold-local frozen reference years 1981–min(2010, fit_end). Tmax >=45°C OR (Tmax >=40°C and departure >=4.5°C).
protocol.limitation: Exploratory historical study: the architecture was informed by previous experiments on some of these years; this is not a new untouched test. Warmup years cannot be independently predicted without earlier data.

coverage.participation: Every April–June row is used in the final refit; later May rows also receive one strictly forward held-out prediction. Early warmup and April/June rows do not have held-out May predictions.

metrics.note: Analytic expected counts; PR-AUC is the no-skill prevalence reference; F1 is derived from expected counts.

source_decision.recommendation: Retain ERA5 as the assessed source and NASA POWER as an independent robustness check; neither is established as more accurate against Nagpur station truth.
source_decision.rationale: ERA5 preserves the existing local-day proxy and supplies the audited assessed inputs. A larger score on NASA-defined labels does not establish better prediction of ERA5 labels or official warnings.
confounders: NASA UTC and ERA5 Asia/Kolkata days differ.
NASA 2m and ERA5 10m wind differ even with common feature names.
The new common 52-input study differs from the original 26-input replay; model versions remain separate.
source_decision.validation_needed: Matched Nagpur station observations and official dated declarations before selecting a source for operational warning accuracy.

metric_note: Accuracy=(TP+TN)/N. Precision=TP/(TP+FP). A fair coin has expected accuracy 50%; the always-negative baseline can be much higher for rare events.
